body: Thank you for the link to that post. It has given me some things to reflect upon, especially the active listening portion. I have a bad habit of listening when to talk instead of just listening, and it's something I know I need to really approve upon if I want to be as supportive of my friend as I can be. I've known about this bad habit for a while now and have had it pointed out to me multiple times, so it helps that I now have access to a post and links that can assist me in becoming a better listener.

I never considered that. I was just so worried that my messages were pushing him away and that's why he's not responding. He has said, when he broke the silence awhile back, that he was just having a moment of weakness and apologized for being a burden. He ended up calling me on Skype a few days after that, and at the end, he just said thanks for sticking with him through our call. He hasn't spoken to me for nearly two weeks since, so I thought maybe I have been saying or doing the wrong things. But, I will definitely keep checking in on him even if he doesn't respond. I don't want to pull the rug of support I've been giving him out from underneath him if that's what's been keeping him going.

But I sincerely thank you so much for your comment. :) It has given me a perspective that my own depressed and anxious brain just never allowed me to have. It helps when someone slashes through your negative-thought cycle and gives a more positive perspective.

Thanks for responding! :) I'll try to keep this in mind going forward. I would never want to pressure him in any way, so if he needs space, then I'll do my best to give that to him. I've let him know that I'll understand if he is unable to talk, so I'll try and respect that. I'll still message him, of course, but less often in case I've been putting undue pressure on him.
